topic: Evidence base for the fixed authored Trace ML course
verificationNote: The original 95 URLs were reported live with HTTP 200 by one of five research lanes or three direct-resource audits on 2026-08-02. Nine claim-specific correction and teaching-design sources were live-validated on 2026-08-03. Three exact sources for the ridge objective, demographic parity, and equality of opportunity were live-validated on 2026-08-04. This registry preserves report-level metadata; unknown exact dates are null or qualified rather than inferred.

sources.title: Machine Learning Crash Course
sources.dateNote: HTTP Last-Modified date reported by the curriculum research lane.
keyInsights: Orders linear regression before logistic classification, data/generalization, neural networks, embeddings, and later production topics.
Combines short explanations, concept checks, visualizations, and browser exercises.
limitations: Breadth and short exercises do not by themselves establish mechanism understanding.
Its published order is evidence for a spine, not validation of Trace ML's full lesson design.
designImplications: Use the foundational ordering as one input to the fixed spine.
Place its short readings after local authored checkpoints rather than using them as gates.

sources.title: CS229: Machine Learning, Summer 2026
sources.dateNote: HTTP Last-Modified date reported by the curriculum research lane.
keyInsights: Moves from least squares and optimization through evaluation, classification, classical models, neural networks, transformers, dimensionality reduction, reinforcement learning, and generative models.
Pairs a mathematically rigorous sequence with problem sets.
limitations: Assumes probability, multivariable calculus, linear algebra, and Python.
Current problem sets were reported as access-restricted.
designImplications: Preserve optimization and evaluation foundations before advanced topics.
Reduce prerequisite load and expose mechanisms visually for the Trace ML audience.

sources.title: MIT 6.390 Introduction to Machine Learning, Fall 2026
sources.dateNote: The research lane described this as a current Fall 2026 draft; an exact update day was not established.
keyInsights: Uses a recurring lecture, team-lab, and pen-and-paper recitation rhythm.
limitations: The public topic calendar was still locked during verification.
It cannot support claims about exact topic order.
designImplications: Use its delivery rhythm as evidence for alternating explanation, collaborative manipulation, and derivation.
Do not cite it as evidence for Trace ML's lesson sequence.

sources.title: MIT 6.S191 Introduction to Deep Learning, 2026
sources.dateNote: HTTP Last-Modified date reported by the curriculum research lane.
keyInsights: Covers deep learning, sequence modeling, vision, generative modeling, reinforcement learning, LLM fine-tuning, safety, and science applications.
Includes software labs and a project.
limitations: It is a deep-learning course rather than a general ML foundation.
Elementary calculus and linear algebra are assumed.
designImplications: Use it to bound modern post-foundation scope.
Do not move deep-learning applications ahead of loss, optimization, and generalization.

sources.title: CMU 10-301/601 Introduction to Machine Learning, Fall 2025
sources.dateNote: Course term is Fall 2025; the page-update date was reported as 2026-01-09.
keyInsights: Progresses from function approximation and classical models through optimization, feature engineering, neural networks, transformers, reinforcement learning, and unsupervised learning.
Uses written work, programming, quizzes, exams, and recitations.
limitations: Requires substantial programming, probability, statistics, and mathematical maturity.
The page is not a 2026 course offering.
designImplications: Pair conceptual derivation with implementation and diagnosis.
Provide smaller, more guided specimens than this university course expects.

sources.title: Dive into Deep Learning
sources.dateNote: The research lane reported a 2023 site build and repository HEAD dated 2024-03-16.
keyInsights: Uses runnable notebooks and often moves from from-scratch implementations to concise framework APIs.
Provides a broad progression from preliminaries and linear models through modern deep learning.
limitations: Its visible build provenance is older than the current 2026 course sources.
Advanced breadth can outpace mechanism consolidation.
designImplications: Adopt the from-scratch-then-library progression.
Use current official documentation to verify framework details.

sources.title: Machine Learning in Python with scikit-learn
sources.dateNote: HTTP Last-Modified date reported by the curriculum research lane.
keyInsights: Focuses on predictive pipelines, model selection, tuning, linear models, trees, ensembles, and evaluation.
Provides named exercises, solutions, quizzes, and executable notebooks.
limitations: Assumes basic Python and recommends NumPy, pandas, and Matplotlib.
API-first material is not ideal for first mechanism discovery.
designImplications: Introduce it during preprocessing, evaluation, cross-validation, and model selection.
Keep mechanism work local before exposing library abstractions.

sources.title: Berkeley CS189 Introduction to Machine Learning, Spring 2026
sources.dateNote: HTTP Last-Modified date reported by the curriculum research lane.
keyInsights: Connects data mechanics, probability, regression, classification, optimization, bias-variance, neural networks, transformers, and applications.
Homework combines derivation and coding.
limitations: Prerequisites in calculus, linear algebra, probability, discrete mathematics, and Python are strong.
designImplications: Preserve theory-code pairing while reducing mathematical compression.
Keep transformer content after optimization and backpropagation.

sources.title: Harvard CS1810 Machine Learning, Spring 2026
sources.dateNote: HTTP Last-Modified date reported by the curriculum research lane.
keyInsights: Places evaluation and validation early, after kNN and linear regression, then covers optimization, classification, features, neural networks, trees, unsupervised and sequential models.
Uses theory/programming homework and solved weekly sections.
limitations: Assumes nontrivial Python, probability, calculus, and linear algebra.
Survey pace is faster than mechanism-first pacing.
designImplications: Teach data splitting and evaluation before extensive model comparison.
Use solved examples next to matched practice.

sources.title: Understanding Deep Learning, version 5.0.3
sources.dateNote: The lane reported PDF date 2026-02-09 and site Last-Modified 2026-07-18.
keyInsights: Moves from supervised learning, networks, loss, training, and gradients to generalization, architectures, generative models, reinforcement learning, theory, and ethics.
Includes chapter problems, interactive figures, and many fill-in-code notebooks.
limitations: The center of gravity is deep learning rather than a balanced introductory ML course.
Later chapters require more mathematics.
designImplications: Use linked figures and fill-in-code patterns after local conceptual traces.
Keep classical evaluation and feature work in the Trace ML spine.

sources.title: PyTorch Learn the Basics
sources.dateNote: Tutorial update date reported as 2026-01-20; docs build was reported as 2026-07-31.
keyInsights: Orders tensors, datasets and loaders, transforms, model construction, autograd, optimization, and model persistence.
Uses executable FashionMNIST notebooks.
limitations: Assumes prior deep-learning concepts.
The research lane found no formal exercise sequence.
designImplications: Introduce framework mechanics only after the learner can trace the underlying computation.
Use it as reference exposure, not progression evidence.

sources.title: Stanford CS231n Deep Learning for Computer Vision, Spring 2026
sources.dateNote: HTTP Last-Modified date reported by the curriculum research lane.
keyInsights: Places linear classifiers and optimization before neural networks, convolution, attention, generative models, and multimodal topics.
Uses written/programming assignments and a project.
limitations: Computer vision is the organizing domain.
Calculus, linear algebra, probability, and Python are assumed.
designImplications: Retain optimization before architectures.
Use its architecture topics only after the core mechanisms.

sources.title: An Introduction to Statistical Learning
sources.dateNote: The Python edition was reported as published in 2023; no exact day was established.
keyInsights: Provides an accessible progression across regression, classification, resampling, regularization, nonlinear methods, trees, deep learning, and unsupervised learning.
Includes labs, notebooks, datasets, and slides.
limitations: It does not establish current modern-topic scope.
The research report did not identify formal prerequisites.
designImplications: Use it to support statistical-learning explanations and labs.
Cross-check rapidly changing tooling against current official docs.

sources.title: Building AI
sources.dateNote: The course was live in 2026, but the research lane found no disclosed revision date.
keyInsights: Moves through optimization, probability, linear and nearest-neighbor methods, overfitting, logistic regression, neural networks, and project framing.
Offers exercises at multiple difficulty levels.
limitations: Revision freshness is unknown.
Higher levels require coding while prerequisite details are light.
designImplications: Use tiered authored practice without allowing the runtime to choose content.
Keep mechanism evidence consistent across difficulty variants.

sources.title: TensorFlow Playground
sources.dateNote: Artifact dates to 2016; HTTP Last-Modified was reported as 2017-03-09.
keyInsights: Supports editing a small neural network and stepping through training while losses and boundaries update.
limitations: Encourages test-set peeking and simultaneous parameter changes if unguided.
Toy boundaries can be overgeneralized.
designImplications: Use seeded presets only after held-out generalization is taught.
Require one intervention, a committed prediction, and preserved initialization.

sources.title: Test-Enhanced Learning: Taking Memory Tests Improves Long-Term Retention
sources.dateNote: Canonical title, venue, publisher, and publication date were verified from DOI metadata on 2026-08-03.
keyInsights: Restudy aided immediate performance, while retrieval practice produced better retention after longer delays.
limitations: The study does not validate a complete digital-course loop.
Task and population boundaries apply.
designImplications: Include delayed authored retrieval checks.
Do not treat immediate fluency as durable understanding.

sources.title: Retrieval Practice Consistently Benefits Student Learning: a Systematic Review of Applied Research in Schools and Classrooms
sources.dateNote: Canonical title, venue, publisher, and publication date were verified from DOI metadata on 2026-08-03.
keyInsights: Across 50 classroom experiments, a majority of reported effects were medium or large.
limitations: Only a small share of experiments came from non-WEIRD countries.
Effects do not determine one implementation pattern.
designImplications: Use retrieval as one evidence channel.
Plan broader learner testing before claiming generality.

sources.title: Transfer of test-enhanced learning: Meta-analytic review and synthesis
sources.dateNote: Canonical title, venue, publisher, and publication date were verified from DOI metadata on 2026-08-03.
keyInsights: Reported a positive average transfer benefit, with strong dependence on elaboration, response congruence, and initial success.
limitations: Bias-adjusted estimates can be much smaller.
Transfer is conditional rather than automatic.
designImplications: Require explicit structural mapping in transfer tasks.
Avoid claiming that retrieval alone guarantees far transfer.

sources.title: Guessing as a learning intervention: A meta-analytic review of the prequestion effect
sources.dateNote: Canonical title, venue, publisher, and publication date were verified from DOI metadata on 2026-08-03.
keyInsights: Found a moderate benefit for specifically prequestioned material and little general benefit for untested material.
limitations: The effect does not justify broad claims about all subsequent content.
designImplications: Make predictions narrow and concept-aligned.
Do not use a prequestion as evidence for unrelated understanding.

sources.title: ManyClasses 2: The effects of prequestions on media interactions and learning
sources.publisher: Journal of Educational Psychology / American Psychological Association
sources.dateNote: Canonical title, venue, publisher, and publication date were verified from DOI metadata on 2026-08-03.
keyInsights: In a large multi-class experiment, delayed performance improved on prequestioned content.
Prior knowledge moderated effects and some learners disengaged.
limitations: Prequestioning was not uniformly beneficial.
It does not validate Trace ML's full predict stage.
designImplications: Keep predictions low stakes and tightly aligned.
Provide an authored re-entry path for learners who disengage.

sources.title: The benefit of generating errors during learning
sources.publisher: Journal of Experimental Psychology: General / American Psychological Association
sources.dateNote: Canonical title, venue, publisher, and publication date were verified from DOI metadata on 2026-08-03.
keyInsights: Generating an error followed by corrective feedback outperformed reading and incorrect-choice conditions.
Learners misjudged the effective condition as worse.
limitations: Effects depend on corrective feedback and task context.
Learner preference is not a learning-outcome measure.
designImplications: Capture a prediction before reveal and immediately surface the discrepancy.
Do not interpret wrong predictions as failure to progress.

sources.title: Conditions for Effective Learning Without Upfront Instruction: How Practice with Feedback Supports Memory, Generalization, Motivation, and Metacognition
sources.dateNote: Canonical title, venue, publisher, and publication date were verified from DOI metadata on 2026-08-03.
keyInsights: Practice plus answer feedback improved memory.
Explanatory feedback and sufficient prior knowledge were needed for generalization.
limitations: The result does not establish correctness or safety of automated feedback.
Prior-knowledge dependence limits universal application.
designImplications: Author explanatory feedback, not answer-only feedback.
Use prerequisite repair before demanding generalization.

sources.title: Learning from Examples: Instructional Principles from the Worked Examples Research
sources.publisher: Review of Educational Research / American Educational Research Association
sources.dateNote: Canonical title, venue, publisher, and publication date were verified from DOI metadata on 2026-08-03.
keyInsights: Effective examples integrate representations, expose deep structure, vary surface features, and sit near matched practice.
limitations: The review predates current interactive and AI-assisted environments.
designImplications: Place an integrated analogous example next to a matched task.
Link equations, visual state, and data rather than splitting them across screens.

sources.title: Structuring the Transition From Example Study to Problem Solving in Cognitive Skill Acquisition: A Cognitive Load Perspective
sources.dateNote: Canonical title, venue, publisher, and publication date were verified from DOI metadata on 2026-08-03.
keyInsights: Supports moving from complete worked solutions toward increasingly incomplete steps as schemas develop.
limitations: Fading is not necessarily monotonic or irreversible.
The evidence does not prescribe one UI.
designImplications: Author graduated completion tasks.
Allow deterministic scaffolds to return when later evidence is fragile.

sources.title: The Expertise Reversal Effect
sources.dateNote: Canonical title, venue, publisher, and publication date were verified from DOI metadata on 2026-08-03.
keyInsights: Guidance useful to novices can become redundant or harmful as expertise grows.
limitations: Expertise must be established from independent evidence rather than confidence or speed.
designImplications: Offer authored compact paths for demonstrated prerequisites.
Do not let a chatbot infer expertise or hide fixed material.

sources.title: A Meta-analysis of the Worked Examples Effect on Mathematics Performance
sources.dateNote: Canonical title, venue, publisher, and publication date were verified from DOI metadata on 2026-08-03.
keyInsights: Reported a moderate mathematics benefit for worked examples.
Correct examples were strongest, while generic self-explanation prompts negatively moderated effects.
limitations: Mathematics findings do not automatically transfer to all ML tasks.
designImplications: Use specific causal explanation prompts.
Do not append generic reflection to every worked example.

sources.title: Inducing Self-Explanation: a Meta-Analysis
sources.dateNote: Canonical title, venue, publisher, and publication date were verified from DOI metadata on 2026-08-03.
keyInsights: Found a positive average effect for prompted self-explanation across tasks and subjects.
Design variation was substantial.
limitations: An average effect does not identify the best prompt for ML mechanisms.
designImplications: Use explanation prompts tied to causal chains, boundaries, and competing accounts.
Evaluate prompts lesson by lesson.

sources.title: Eliciting Self-Explanations Improves Understanding
sources.dateNote: Canonical title, venue, publisher, and publication date were verified from DOI metadata on 2026-08-03.
keyInsights: Prompted explanation improved mental-model quality and complex inference in the reported study.
limitations: The sample was reported as 24 learners.
The task was not an interactive ML course.
designImplications: Ask for mechanism explanations rather than labels.
Do not overstate generality from a small foundational study.

sources.title: Focus on Formative Feedback
sources.publisher: Review of Educational Research / American Educational Research Association
sources.dateNote: Canonical title, venue, publisher, and publication date were verified from DOI metadata on 2026-08-03.
keyInsights: Feedback is most useful when specific, supportive, task-focused, and actionable.
Timing and learner/task characteristics interact.
limitations: The review does not prescribe automated feedback generation.
One timing rule does not fit every task.
designImplications: Author feedback against visible task evidence.
Keep the chatbot out of grading and feedback policy.

sources.title: The Power of Feedback Revisited: A Meta-Analysis of Educational Feedback Research
sources.dateNote: Canonical title, venue, publisher, and publication date were verified from DOI metadata on 2026-08-03.
keyInsights: Found a positive average feedback effect with substantial heterogeneity.
Information content mattered more than feedback as a generic label.
limitations: Heterogeneity makes a single feedback recipe unsafe.
designImplications: Specify what each feedback message should change in the learner's model.
Test feedback content rather than counting messages.

sources.title: Similarity matters: A meta-analysis of interleaved learning and its moderators
sources.dateNote: Canonical title, venue, publisher, and publication date were verified from DOI metadata on 2026-08-03.
keyInsights: Reported positive average interleaving effects, including mathematics, with stronger value for similar categories requiring discrimination.
Blocking was better for some verbal material.
limitations: Interleaving is not universally beneficial.
designImplications: Interleave neighboring ML mechanisms after first schema formation.
Do not interleave every reading or vocabulary item.

sources.title: Cognitive Load During Problem Solving: Effects on Learning
sources.dateNote: Canonical title, venue, publisher, and publication date were verified from DOI metadata on 2026-08-03.
keyInsights: Unguided means-ends problem solving can consume capacity needed for schema acquisition.
limitations: The theory alone does not specify a complete course design.
Modern interactive contexts require additional evidence.
designImplications: Avoid unaided discovery in early labs.
Constrain each manipulation to one mechanism and visible state.

sources.title: Cognitive load theory, educational research, and instructional design: some food for thought
sources.dateNote: Canonical title, venue, publisher, and online publication date were verified from DOI metadata on 2026-08-03; the issue publication year is 2010.
keyInsights: Identifies unresolved conceptual, measurement, and application problems in cognitive-load theory.
limitations: It is a critique, not a replacement instructional recipe.
designImplications: Treat cognitive load as a design constraint, not a universal explanatory score.
Validate interfaces with learners instead of inferring load from visual simplicity.

sources.title: Meta-Analysis of Inquiry-Based Learning
sources.publisher: Review of Educational Research / American Educational Research Association
sources.dateNote: Canonical title, venue, publisher, and publication date were verified from DOI metadata on 2026-08-03.
keyInsights: Guidance improved learning and successful inquiry performance on average.
limitations: The evidence does not validate free-form exploration.
Guidance forms and domains vary.
designImplications: Provide authored hypotheses, comparison prompts, and controlled variables.
Treat random slider use as activity, not evidence.

sources.title: Computer Simulations to Support Science Instruction and Learning: A critical review of the literature
sources.publisher: International Journal of Science Education / Taylor & Francis
sources.dateNote: Canonical title, venue, publisher, and publication date were verified from DOI metadata on 2026-08-03.
keyInsights: Simulations work best with support, reflection, supplementation, and productive conflict rather than free-form use.
limitations: The reviewed simulations were not specifically ML visualizations.
designImplications: Pair every visual lab with prediction, exact comparison, and explanation.
Keep external interactives optional exposure.

sources.title: When and where do we apply what we learn?: A taxonomy for far transfer
sources.dateNote: Canonical title, venue, publisher, and publication date were verified from DOI metadata on 2026-08-03.
keyInsights: Shows that transfer distance spans multiple dimensions and should not be treated as one general effect.
limitations: The taxonomy does not specify a single assessment format.
designImplications: Label which context, representation, response, and time dimensions change.
Test near transfer before claims of far transfer.

sources.title: Analogical encoding facilitates knowledge transfer in negotiation
sources.dateNote: Canonical title, venue, publisher, and publication date were verified from DOI metadata on 2026-08-03; the prior Memory & Cognition venue was incorrect.
keyInsights: Comparing structurally equivalent cases increased later transfer in the reported experiments.
limitations: The population and tasks differ from an introductory ML course.
The result does not guarantee far transfer.
designImplications: Author paired surface-different cases before an uncued transfer.
Require learners to state the shared deep structure.

sources.title: Effectiveness of Mastery Learning Programs: A Meta-Analysis
sources.publisher: Review of Educational Research / American Educational Research Association
sources.dateNote: Canonical title, venue, publisher, and publication date were verified from DOI metadata on 2026-08-03.
keyInsights: Reported positive achievement effects, including benefits for weaker students.
Mastery approaches could require more time and lower self-paced completion.
limitations: Interventions bundle thresholds, feedback, repetition, and time.
The evidence does not validate a universal percentage cutoff.
designImplications: Use multiple evidence channels instead of one score.
Track additional time and attrition as costs.

sources.title: Mastery Learning for Health Professionals Using Technology-Enhanced Simulation
sources.dateNote: Canonical title, venue, publisher, and publication date were verified from DOI metadata on 2026-08-03.
keyInsights: Simulation mastery interventions showed large skill effects against no intervention in the reviewed medical-education literature.
Direct comparisons with nonmastery instruction were scarce and mastery took longer.
limitations: Domain transfer to ML is uncertain.
Few studies isolated mastery from other instructional components.
designImplications: Do not cite mastery evidence as proof of Trace ML's gates.
Measure time cost and compare against an active instructional baseline.

sources.title: Learning Versus Performance
sources.publisher: Perspectives on Psychological Science / SAGE Publications
sources.dateNote: Canonical title, venue, publisher, and publication date were verified from DOI metadata on 2026-08-03.
keyInsights: Immediate performance can be an unreliable, and sometimes inverse, indicator of durable retention and transfer.
limitations: The review does not define a complete ML-course evidence model.
designImplications: Separate immediate, independent, transfer, and delayed evidence.
Never infer understanding from completion speed or confidence alone.

sources.title: Refutation Text Facilitates Learning: a Meta-Analysis of Between-Subjects Experiments
sources.dateNote: Canonical title, venue, publisher, and publication date were verified from DOI metadata on 2026-08-03.
keyInsights: Explicit refutation text produced a moderate average benefit across the reviewed comparisons.
limitations: Text effects do not establish the best refutation interaction for ML labs.
designImplications: Name the nearest misconception and contrast it with observable evidence.
Recheck the distinction in a later varied case.

sources.title: Scientific knowledge suppresses but does not supplant earlier intuitions
sources.dateNote: Canonical title, venue, publisher, and publication date were verified from DOI metadata on 2026-08-03.
keyInsights: Reported evidence that scientific knowledge can suppress rather than fully replace intuitive theories.
limitations: The study spans science concepts rather than ML misconceptions.
Correct answers may not reveal latent conflict.
designImplications: Use delayed and varied discrimination checks.
Do not erase a misconception flag after one correct response.

sources.title: Students' Misconceptions and Other Difficulties in Introductory Programming
sources.publisher: ACM Transactions on Computing Education / Association for Computing Machinery
sources.dateNote: Canonical title, venue, publisher, and publication date were verified from DOI metadata on 2026-08-03.
keyInsights: Programming difficulty spans syntax, concepts, strategy, mental models, prior knowledge, and development environments.
limitations: The review is not specific to ML code or browser Python runtimes.
designImplications: Diagnose code failures by category.
Avoid treating a failed program as proof that the ML mechanism is misunderstood.

sources.title: An exploratory study on fade-in versus fade-out scaffolding for novice programmers in online collaborative programming settings
sources.publisher: Journal of Computing in Higher Education / Springer Nature
sources.dateNote: Canonical title, venue, publisher, and publication date were verified from DOI metadata on 2026-08-03.
keyInsights: In the reported collaborative-programming study, fade-in support outperformed fade-out support.
limitations: The study was exploratory with a reported sample of 90.
Collaborative programming conditions differ from Trace ML.
designImplications: Do not assume scaffolding should only decrease.
Allow authored supports to reappear based on deterministic evidence.

sources.title: Reevaluating the relationship between explaining, tracing, and writing skills in CS1 in a replication study
sources.dateNote: Canonical title, venue, publisher, and publication date were verified from DOI metadata on 2026-08-03.
keyInsights: Explaining, tracing, and writing code were correlated in a large learner sample.
limitations: The study explicitly could not establish an ideal instructional order.
designImplications: Treat Trace ML's sequence as a hypothesis.
Measure separate explain, trace, modify, and write outcomes.

sources.title: A Visual Exploration of Gaussian Processes
sources.dateNote: Published 2019-04-02 and reported modified 2021-12-17.
keyInsights: Coordinates slider changes across equations, samples, and uncertainty views.
limitations: Smooth visuals can naturalize kernel and prior assumptions.
Exploration has no built-in comprehension gate.
designImplications: Borrow linked representations for backpropagation and hidden-state lessons.
Always pair manipulation with a prediction and explanation.

sources.title: Grokking
sources.dateNote: Publication year reported; exact day was not established.
keyInsights: Uses a scrubbable training timeline to connect loss, representations, and generalization.
limitations: An exceptional phase transition may look normal or guaranteed.
designImplications: Place only after ordinary training dynamics.
Show multiple seeds and non-grokking controls.

sources.title: Seeing Theory: Basic Probability
sources.dateNote: Publication year reported; exact day was not established.
keyInsights: Connects repeated trials to sample and distribution behavior through direct manipulation.
limitations: IID and stationarity assumptions can remain implicit.
Finite-sample variation may be mistaken for a convergence guarantee.
designImplications: Show repeated sampling and visible uncertainty in early data lessons.
Name independence and stationarity assumptions.

sources.title: But what is a neural network?
sources.dateNote: Publication date reported by the visual-artifact research lane.

media.title: But what is a neural network? | Deep learning chapter 1

keyInsights: Uses progressive animation and current interactive checks to build neural-network intuition.
limitations: Visual fluency can substitute for understanding.
Brain analogies and feature-detector narratives can be interpreted too literally.
designImplications: Place after a local hidden-unit prediction.
Require transfer to a non-image example.

sources.title: Interactive Visualization of Linear Regression
sources.dateNote: Publication date reported by the visual-artifact research lane.
keyInsights: Allows points to be added, dragged, and removed while residuals, fit, and R-squared update.
limitations: May imply analysts should alter observations.
R-squared can be misread as causality, model quality, or generalization.
designImplications: Rebuild the useful residual linking locally.
Require an outlier prediction and explicitly separate fit from causality and held-out performance.

sources.title: A Visual Introduction to Machine Learning, Part 1
sources.dateNote: Publication year reported; the canonical non-www URL was live during verification.
keyInsights: Uses scroll-driven staged construction to make decision-tree steps inspectable.
limitations: A clean dataset can make training look like discovery of an obvious boundary.
designImplications: Use staged reveal for tree mechanics.
Follow with noise, ambiguity, and a counterexample.

sources.title: K-Means Explorable
sources.dateNote: Publication year reported; publisher identity and exact day were not established by the research report.
keyInsights: Combines a manual objective, deterministic algorithm stepping, assumptions, local minima, scaling, and outliers.
limitations: Geometric simplicity does not automatically transfer to other objectives.
designImplications: Use its objective-to-step-to-failure architecture for gradient descent.
State where the analogy stops.

sources.title: Train, Test, and Validation Sets
sources.dateNote: First-commit provenance reported by the visual-artifact research lane; the collection was active in 2026.
keyInsights: Links feature choices, classifier boundaries, and dataset splits.
limitations: Repeated selection makes simple claims that validation or test accuracy is unbiased too strong.
designImplications: Teach explicit train, validation, and test roles.
Show uncertainty and contamination from repeated selection.

sources.title: PRIMM
sources.publisher: Raspberry Pi Computing Education Research Centre
sources.dateNote: Modification date reported by the code-pedagogy research lane.
keyInsights: Organizes beginner code work as Predict, Run, Investigate, Modify, and Make, beginning from working code.
The associated research programme included a reported 500-pupil multiweek study.
limitations: PRIMM is general programming pedagogy, not an ML-mechanism curriculum.
The page summary does not validate Trace ML's complete code sequence.
designImplications: Begin code tasks from runnable specimens.
Require predictions and investigation before modification.

sources.title: Linear Regression: Loss
sources.dateNote: Update date reported by the code-pedagogy research lane.
keyInsights: Provides a short official treatment of residuals and loss before model fitting code.
limitations: A short reading cannot demonstrate that the learner can trace per-example loss.
It is external exposure, not a gate.
designImplications: Place after the local two-prediction loss comparison.
Introduce the first pure-Python specimen only after this mechanism is locally visible.

sources.title: Gradient Descent
sources.type: official course module with embedded video
sources.dateNote: Update date reported by the code-pedagogy research lane.

media.title: Machine Learning Crash Course: Gradient Descent

keyInsights: Explains gradient descent in the linear-regression sequence before an interactive exercise.
limitations: It does not prove that a learner can predict or repair an update loop.
designImplications: Place after a local update-direction prediction.
Follow with a small authored loop and learning-rate failure.

sources.title: Learning PyTorch with Examples
sources.dateNote: Update date reported by the code-pedagogy research lane.
keyInsights: Moves from manual NumPy forward and backward passes to tensors, autograd, and neural-network modules.
limitations: The tutorial assumes enough prior concept knowledge to interpret the code.
Framework details can change.
designImplications: Mirror its manual-to-autograd abstraction path.
Pin and test the local runtime independently of the external tutorial.

sources.title: What is NumPy?
sources.dateNote: Documentation build date reported by the code-pedagogy research lane.
keyInsights: Explains vectorization, multidimensional arrays, efficiency, and reduced code as reasons to move beyond Python sequences.
limitations: It is a library overview, not an ML lesson.
Performance claims depend on operation and context.
designImplications: Introduce NumPy when shape, batching, or vectorization becomes visible subject matter.
Do not begin the course with opaque array operations.

sources.title: LPITutor: an LLM based personalized intelligent tutoring system using RAG and prompt engineering
sources.dateNote: Canonical DOI, title, venue, publisher, authors, and publication date were verified from the PubMed Central citation metadata on 2026-08-03.
keyInsights: Provides current evidence relevant to grounding educational responses in retrieved learning material.
limitations: It does not validate Trace ML's exact page-grounded Q&A feature.
A tutoring study cannot justify giving the chatbot curriculum authority.
designImplications: Keep factual answers restricted to approved page evidence.
Evaluate grounding separately from learning outcomes.

sources.title: ALCE citation evaluation
sources.dateNote: Publication year reported; exact title wording was not supplied in the research report.
keyInsights: Provides evaluation concepts for citation correctness and completeness in generated answers.
limitations: General citation benchmarks do not guarantee educational usefulness.
Web-scale answering differs from an allowlisted page corpus.
designImplications: Measure citation recall and precision for factual claims.
Reject answers with unsupported atomic claims.

sources.title: ReClaim sentence-level citations
sources.dateNote: Publication year reported; exact title wording was not supplied in the research report.
keyInsights: Supports sentence-level alignment between generated claims and cited evidence.
limitations: Citation alignment does not establish pedagogical quality or factual truth beyond the corpus.

sources.title: torch.autograd.gradcheck.gradcheck
sources.dateNote: The current stable PyTorch API page and its analytical-versus-finite-difference contract were live-validated on 2026-08-03. The shorter torch.autograd.gradcheck URL returned 404.
keyInsights: Checks analytical gradients against numerical finite-difference approximations for eligible floating-point or complex inputs.
limitations: Passing applies only to tested inputs, tolerances, and differentiability conditions; lower precision, nondifferentiable points, and overlapping memory can invalidate the comparison.
designImplications: Test several signed scalar states and describe agreement as implementation support, not proof that the model or objective is correct.

sources.title: torch.optim.SGD
sources.dateNote: The current stable PyTorch API page, momentum equations, and first-buffer convention were live-validated on 2026-08-03.
keyInsights: Documents stochastic gradient descent with optional momentum and the PyTorch convention v = momentum * v + gradient before the parameter step.
limitations: PyTorch initializes the first momentum buffer from the first gradient and explicitly differs from some formulations; overshoot after a sign change is possible rather than guaranteed.
designImplications: Name the exact convention used by the executable specimen and expose velocity beside each parameter update.

sources.title: torch.optim.Adam
sources.dateNote: The current stable PyTorch API page, moment updates, bias correction, and parameter equation were live-validated on 2026-08-03.
keyInsights: Documents exponential running averages of gradients and squared gradients, their bias corrections, and the epsilon-stabilized parameter update.
limitations: Weight decay, decoupled weight decay, AMSGrad, and maximize alter the algorithm; Adam does not guarantee generalization or universal convergence.
designImplications: Require the learner to implement the bias-corrected parameter update and verify both moment states across signed gradients.

keyInsights: Defines scaled dot-product attention as softmax of scaled query-key products applied to value vectors.
limitations: The operation specifies intermediate routing, not a causal explanation of a final prediction or a complete modern transformer implementation.

sources.title: Retrieval Practice in Stepwise Worked Examples Improves Learning
sources.dateNote: The DOI, Crossref record, OpenAlex record, and open Utrecht University repository abstract were live-validated on 2026-08-04.
keyInsights: In a randomized study of 164 adults, prompting learners to retrieve each upcoming step in later isomorphic worked examples improved one-week recall and problem-solving performance relative to stepwise example study without retrieval prompts.
limitations: The study used two triplets of isomorphic examples with adult online participants; it does not validate Trace ML's complete lesson sequence or immediate choice questions.
designImplications: Present a complete worked mechanism, then require retrieval on an analogous case whose decisive values and answer were not already disclosed.

sources.title: sklearn.linear_model.Ridge
sources.dateNote: The current stable API page, objective equation, and L2 regularization-strength definition were live-validated on 2026-08-04.
keyInsights: Ridge minimizes squared error plus alpha times the squared L2 norm of the coefficient vector, so a nonzero alpha changes the fitting objective rather than acting only as a numerical division guard.
limitations: The API covers a general estimator and multiple solvers; Trace ML uses a fixed tiny penalty and its own deterministic elimination routine for a small visual mechanism.
designImplications: Describe the fixed 0.000001 term as a small coefficient-size penalty that changes the objective and selects a reproducible solution when the rows do not uniquely determine coefficients.

sources.title: Fairness: Demographic parity
sources.dateNote: The official page, overall acceptance-rate comparison, benefits, and limitations were live-validated on 2026-08-04.
keyInsights: Demographic parity compares overall positive-decision or acceptance rates across demographic groups without conditioning on individual qualification or the outcome label.
limitations: Equal selection rates can overlook differences within groups and do not by themselves determine whether a system is fair in context.
designImplications: Compute group selection rates from all cases, report the observed gap without inventing a universal tolerance, and keep the metric separate from stakeholder judgment.

sources.title: Fairness: Equality of opportunity
sources.dateNote: The official page, qualified-subset acceptance comparison, benefits, and limitations were live-validated on 2026-08-04.
keyInsights: Equality of opportunity compares positive-decision rates within the actually positive or otherwise qualified subset of each group, corresponding to a true-positive-rate comparison.
limitations: The metric depends on trustworthy outcome labels and a meaningful preferred outcome; equal true-positive rates alone do not settle all fairness consequences.
designImplications: Compute true-positive rates only from actually positive cases, compare their observed gap with the selection-rate gap, and retain the label-quality and stakeholder-context boundary.

sources.title: Prerequisites and prework
sources.dateNote: The official prerequisite page, including its Python, NumPy, algebra, linear algebra, statistics, and optional calculus expectations, was live-validated on 2026-08-04.
keyInsights: A course described as serving beginners can still require prior Python, NumPy, algebra, statistics, and optional calculus, so a genuinely from-zero course must author those missing foundations rather than silently inherit them.
limitations: The page inventories prerequisites for Google's course; it does not establish one ideal order or teaching method for Trace ML's zero-onramp.
designImplications: Teach the exact Python and mathematical notation used in Lesson 00 before asking the learner to predict, manipulate, explain, transfer, or repair code.

sources.title: An Informal Introduction to Python
sources.dateNote: The Python 3.14.6 tutorial sections on arithmetic, assignment, lists, and len were live-validated on 2026-08-04.
keyInsights: Python assignment binds names to values, square brackets construct lists, arithmetic expressions can be evaluated directly, and len reports the number of items in a sequence.
limitations: The tutorial is a language reference and introduction, not evidence that one syntax sequence is instructionally optimal or a guide to NumPy arrays.
designImplications: Define assignment, lists, function calls, loops, and return in plain language before the first editable Python specimen.
